root_causes.description: The checkout container was repeatedly killed and restarted (3 restarts in the 5-minute window, K8s event 'Killing: Stopping container checkout'), taking the service down and producing a 92% error rate on checkout server spans. CPU (0.05 cores) and memory (~100MB) remained flat and normal, ruling out resource exhaustion as the kill trigger.

evidence.query_or_id: Killing: Stopping container checkout (count=1); Started: Started container checkout (count=1)
evidence.observed_value: Container checkout killed and restarted during incident window
evidence.expected_baseline: No Killing/BackOff events for checkout pods
memory stable, no OOM pressure (rules out memory_stress)

evidence.observed_value: ERROR trace, 1200ms duration, checkout service during incident window

root_causes.description: Secondary hypothesis: an HTTP abort fault on checkout causing the 92% error rate. Ranked lower because the concurrent restart counter and container kill event make pod crash the more complete explanation.

Least likely: a failure in one of checkout's downstream dependencies (cart, payment, email, shipping, currency, product-catalog) propagating errors. Weakly supported — the error trace duration (1200ms) is unremarkable and the container kill event points to a local checkout fault rather than downstream propagation.

evidence.observed_value: ERROR trace with p95_duration=1200ms on checkout (no extreme latency indicating downstream hang)
evidence.expected_baseline: dependency failures would show long-duration checkout traces with downstream span errors

remediation_steps: Inspect the killed container's exit details: kubectl describe pod <checkout-pod> -n otel-demo and kubectl logs <checkout-pod> --previous -n otel-demo to determine the kill cause (OOMKilled, liveness probe failure, or external kill).
Verify checkout container resource requests/limits and liveness/readiness probe thresholds; adjust if the probe was killing a slow-but-healthy container.
Check for recent deployments/config changes to checkout and roll back if a bad change correlates with the crash window.
Add alerting on kube_pod_container_status_restarts_total for checkout and a PodDisruptionBudget to reduce blast radius of repeated restarts.
Once the pod is stable, confirm checkout error_rate returns to baseline (<0.01) and frontend checkout conversion recovers.
